newsitem.title: FRANCE: French fraud probe widens, hits Bouygues giant.
newsitem.headline: French fraud probe widens, hits Bouygues giant.

text.p: The managing director of a subsidiary of French building giant Bouygues was placed under investigation Thursday in a fraud probe, justice sources said.
Judge Jean-Marie Charpier questioned Philippe Chalendon in Versailles, outside Paris, for alleged misuse of corporate funds, the sources said.
The sources added that Charpier made clear that Bouygues Chairman Martin Bouygues could likewise be brought before him later Thursday as chairman of the Saur subsidiary.
Chalendon is managing director of the maritime branch of Bouygues Offshore.

Police released Patrick Le Lay, the head of private television channel TF1, overnight after the businessmen were summoned Wednesday for questioning in the probe into false invoices involving some 40 companies in the Paris area.
